articles.title: Diablo 4’s Expansion Days Are Over
articles.summary: Diablo 4 won't receive more expansions moving forward, as Blizzard shifts its focus to the newly revealed Diablo 5 instead. As revealed during BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, Diablo 5 is slated to be coming in Spring 2029 and is set 100 years after Diablo 4 in a world where the titular Lord of…
body: That doesn't mean support for Diablo 4 will end anytime soon. It sounds like Diablo 4's seasons will lead into the events of Diablo 5, even though the latter takes place a century later. That gives Blizzard room to set up Diablo 5's story, though Gibson said Blizzard doesn't "have a perfect picture" where it will all go because it wants to see how fans "react season to season."

Diablo 4 is the only Diablo game to have received more than one expansion. Prior to release, Blizzard said it would receive "annual" expansions, though that quickly didn't come to pass. The game's Lord of Hatred expansion was released in April of this year, around a year-and-a-half after Diablo 4's first expansion, Vessel of Hatred.

It's not a new expansion, but Diablo 4 is receiving a new class. The Amazon will join Diablo 4 as a standalone DLC next year. Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, begins September 15, and will see the return of iconic locations, items, Deckard Cain. The iconic Hordadrim will task players with battling memories of the Prime Evils from previous Diablo games, including Diablo himself.
points: Diablo 4 won't receive more expansions moving forward, as Blizzard shifts its focus to the newly revealed Diablo 5 instead.

articles.title: Diablo 5’s Revealed Classes Are Throwbacks To Diablo 3, With One Exception
articles.summary: Diablo 5 isn't coming until Spring 2029, but Blizzard has already revealed three of the game's playable classes. Two of them will be familiar to Diablo 3 fans: the Monk and Demon Hunter. The third will be an all-new class, the Plague Knight.
body: Blizzard revealed plenty of new details about Diablo 5 during a panel and subsequent blog post following the game's cinematic reveal as part of the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony. In addition to the three classes, Blizzard outlined the state of Sanctuary in Diablo 5 and how players will navigate it. Rather than journeying to towns, players will instead build a wandering caravan of survivors in a world that's been destroyed, and currently ruled, by Diablo himself. According to a developer blog post, Diablo 5's world will be "procedural," where terrain, monsters, and points of interest will change in the wake of the Lord of Terror's influence.

As for the survivors that players will call allies, Blizzard said they will serve roles as vendors and companions. Two examples of companions that will accompany players are a former Sister of the Sightless Eye and a lost treasure goblin searching for meaning "in a world where greed has lost its meaning," Blizzard said.
points: Diablo 5 isn't coming until Spring 2029, but Blizzard has already revealed three of the game's playable classes.
Two of them will be familiar to Diablo 3 fans: the Monk and Demon Hunter.

articles.title: Scooby-Doo: Origins Reveals Cute New Photo of the Live-Action Dog
articles.summary: Netflix announced Sunday that production has officially wrapped in Atlanta on their upcoming series Scooby-Doo: Origins. The streaming service also released a new photo of the titular good boy, which can be seen in the image gallery below.
body: Scooby-Doo: Origins marks the first time a real Great Dane has portrayed the beloved canine member of the Mystery Inc. gang.

“During their final summer at camp, old friends Shaggy and Daphne get embroiled in a haunting mystery surrounding a lonely lost Great Dane puppy that may have been a witness to a supernatural murder,” according to the official synopsis.

“Together with the pragmatic and scientific townie, Velma, and the strange, but ever so handsome new kid, Freddy, they set out to solve the case that is pulling each of them into a creepy nightmare that threatens to expose all of their secrets.”
Scooby-Doo: Origins stars Mckenna Grace as “Daphne Blake,” Tanner Hagen as “Shaggy Rogers,” Abby Ryder Fortson as “Velma Dinkley,” Maxwell Jenkins as “Fred Jones.”

articles.title: 'Buddy' is Totally Bonkers, But it Will Never Eclipse My Favorite “I Hate Barney” Thriller
articles.summary: Buddy is about a group of kids featured in a Barney & Friends -like children’s show. They sing songs and learn lessons from Buddy, an adorable orange unicorn (voiced by Keegan-Michael Key).
body: Earlier this year, the indie horror phenomenon Obsession pulled off the impossible: it made more money on its second weekend in theaters than it did in its first. This month, that happened again with another horror film, Buddy, which earned $5.3 million during the weekend of August 28, and then raked in another $5.7 million over Labor Day weekend. While that’s nowhere near Obsession's blockbuster numbers, it’s a big win for a horror flick with a mere $3 million budget.

Buddy ’s premise is fantastic, and its best asset is Buddy himself, who looks, feels, and sounds like a real kiddie-show mascot from the 1990s. However, while the critical acclaim for the film may put me in the minority, I don’t really think it lives up to its ingenious idea. With an adorable, fluffy, killer unicorn at its center, I expected Buddy to be both funny and scary, but it only ever elicited a few chuckles from me, and it was far more gory than scary. I don’t mind gore, but it’s not a substitute for terror or creepiness.
Honestly, the experience of watching Buddy was so disappointing to me that it had me yearning for a far more satisfying takedown of Barney the dinosaur, the 2002 comedy, Death to Smoochy.

articles.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Is Overwatch's Next Big Anime Collaboration
articles.summary: At BlizzCon, Blizzard Entertainment and CD Projekt Red delved into several upcoming collaborations between the two companies. These include Battle.net versions of CD Projekt Red's RPGs, but also a Cyberpunk: Edgerunners collaboration for Overwatch.
body: This new Overwatch collaboration was announced towards the start of BlizzCon 2026's 30 Years of Battle.net panel, we we learned that Cyberpunk collaborations are also on the table for Blizzard, not just The Witcher ones.

Although not a lot was revealed, two pieces of art for it were shown off and confirmed that David from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Talia from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 will get Overwatch cosmetics. We don't know which heroes they will be for yet, though, or if Edgerunners characters like Lucy will get outfits of their own.

Overwatch has crossed over with anime like My Hero Academia, Cowboy Bebop, and One-Punch Man in the past, so the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners crossover seems natural. We'll learn more about this collaboration before it comes to Overwatch sometime in 2027. Before then, Edgerunners 2 will be released on Netflix on Oct. 20, and we learned that Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition is coming to Battle.net in 2026.
points: These include Battle.net versions of CD Projekt Red's RPGs, but also a Cyberpunk: Edgerunners collaboration for Overwatch.

articles.title: Diablo 4's new season brings back Deckard Cain and all three Prime Evils as the game arrives on Switch 2
articles.summary: Diablo 4 's next season, Season of Hell's Legacy, will go live on 15th September to celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary and Nintendo Switch 2 debut.
body: At BlizzCon's opening ceremony, developer Blizzard said the season will be a tribute to three decades of Diablo, built around the return of Deckard Cain and a rematch against all three original Prime Evils: Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto.

Cain's spirit returns to warn players that echoes of the three Prime Evils have resurfaced. Each one's holed up in a location familiar to those who've played the earlier games - Tristram Cathedral, Arreat Summit, the Durance of Hate. Beat one and you get a Soul Splinter, which lets you borrow a bit of that demon's power. The catch is that it also makes you more vulnerable to that same demon.

That's not all, either. Nine new Legacy Uniques also join the game permanently, including a returning Stone of Jordan, alongside a batch of enemy encounters called Waking Nightmares that recreate specific moments from Diablo's past.
The new content is slated to go live at 5.30pm UK time on 15th September.
points: Diablo 4 's next season, Season of Hell's Legacy, will go live on 15th September to celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary and Nintendo Switch 2 debut.

articles.title: 10 Near-Perfect GameCube Games Nobody Played
articles.summary: The Nintendo GameCube is the last time Nintendo made a priority out of competing with the technical specifications offered by its competition, and it did so while shipping everything in a purple box with a handle.
body: Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg was included on the Nintendo GameCube Preview Disc that Nintendo made available during the 2003 holiday season, but that exposure didn’t lead to critical success for Sega. Developed by Sonic Team, the game had unique mechanics that felt like they might have fit naturally in a Sonic Adventure title. Players moved giant eggs around while completing missions and avoiding hazards throughout puzzling stages. Mainstream success may have eluded it, but the game is a fun time when you approach it with the right mindset.

Capcom enjoyed tremendous success and published numerous hits on the GameCube, but Gotcha Force managed to slip under the radar despite offering compelling 3D shooting action. Players went through its lengthy campaign multiple times to unlock a massive fighting force of well-armed toys, which they pitted against squads controlled by up to three other players. The arcade stylings aren’t for everyone, and the camera could have done with some additional refinement. But for players in the mood for something competitive along the lines of Power Stone, there’s a lot to like.

articles.title: Peacock’s Friday the 13th Prequel Is Already Looking Like a Must-Watch
articles.summary: This October is shaping up to be a great time for fans of horror on TV. American Horror Story is returning with a massive crossover in its thirteenth season. Horror power duo Mike Flanagan and Stephen King will premiere a new miniseries adaptation of Carrie on Prime Video.
body: The new trailer focuses on Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) as she integrates into the Crystal Lake community at the local summer camp with her son, Jason. The young boy tragically drowns, sending Pam into a deep depression. She appears haunted by his death and even feels that Jason may still be out there. It's not long before strange circumstances begin occurring in Crystal Lake, including gruesome murders. What's behind the bloodshed is left unsaid.

One of the best parts of the trailer is how much classic horror gore it serves up. The prospect of a prestige miniseries set before one of the most iconic horror movies ever has always been a bit of a strange pitch, but it seems A24 and Peacock aren't shying away from the franchise's bread and butter: expect lots of sex and blood. The trailer notes that the show begins in 1971, which means Jason's death has been moved up from the original movie's version of events in 1957.
points: This October is shaping up to be a great time for fans of horror on TV.

articles.title: Fallout dev Tim Cain says the games industry's volatility is 'always gonna be around': 'What's happening now isn't novel, it isn't new'
articles.summary: I don't know if you've noticed, but the games industry kind of sucks. Despite (and because of) the absurd amount of money games rake in, there's an ungodly degree of consolidation, the RAMpocalypse, and constant, huge waves of layoffs.
body: "Why are things looking particularly bad right now? Well, the simple answer is 'cause they are bad right now," he said in the video. "Correction for [reckless investment during] COVID, hardware costs have shot up—a lot due to AI data centers—but investors are redirecting their money outside of the games industry, in some cases outside of the US … things had to contract. And that means people are gonna get laid off.
"These things will pass. They really will. I know if you're caught up in it, you're thinking, 'this is terrible.' They'll pass. That's the good news. The bad news is, new ones are gonna happen."

Cain was careful in his video to clarify that he understands things are uniquely bad now, but also said that things have been bad and will be bad again. "If you're somebody who got into the games industry in that time period, in the last five or 10 years, and you thought it was going to be a stable job that would see through 30 or 40 years, you assumed incorrectly. You're wrong."

articles.title: Professor Layton studio Level-5's CEO admits using AI to make its digital showcase "more spectacular"
articles.summary: Level-5 president and CEO Akihiro Hino has confirmed that generative AI was used in the studio's recent showcase.
body: As spotted by VGC, fans quickly called out suspected undisclosed AI after the studio's digital showcase debuted last week.

Now, in response to the backlash, Hino has confirmed AI was used to make the presentation footage "more spectacular", admitting: "It appears that some people felt uncomfortable about this, so I deeply apologise".

"I was SO excited when Level-5 announced their big comeback with Professor Layton, Decapolice, Yo-Kai Watch, and more," wrote one fan on X/Twitter. "But seeing this much blatant genAI being used across their games… yeah, this ain't it."

"This time, because we used AI for the footage within the event, it seems that concerns have arisen regarding the content of the works as well, so I would like to provide an explanation," Hino said on X/Twitter (as translated by machine).

articles.title: YouTuber runs onto the stage at Roblox Developers Conference shouting 'We deserve better,' gets tackled and ejected from show
articles.summary: Over the last few days, Roblox's 2026 Developers Conference was held in San Jose, California, and one of Roblox CEO David Baszucki's on-stage introduction's hit something of a hitch.
body: Baszucki played the incident off in the moment, saying "We all get a little excited when RDC comes along, as we just saw." But it was shared online by X user bearpuppyrbx, prompting a quote-repost from Mathieo himself—"just got kicked out #rdc26 💔," he wrote. He explained his stunt the same day in a short YouTube video uploaded to his channel.

"I know there's a lot of people that really love RDC, and I'm glad people are enjoying themselves," he said in the video. "My issue isn't with the people. I just do believe that Roblox [Corporation] isn't as dumb as they say they are … everybody's saying they don't want AI. Everybody's saying they don't want these faces messed up. Everybody wants better child safety.
"Every single slow year of progress is just another year where children are actually affected."

Roblox's dubious child safety measures have been criticized for a number of years. It has recently introduced child accounts in an attempt to address the issue, the US Senate is actively investigating the platform, and legislation like the EU's Digital Services Act aim to force Roblox Corporation's hand in protecting minors.

articles.title: My favourite soundtrack of 2026 so far is tucked in one of this year's biggest sleeper hits
articles.summary: Critical Hit. Welcome to Critical Hit, where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.
body: I have not been able to stop thinking about Big Walk since I finished the game alongside six of my friends last month. What I had anticipated to be a relatively okay, quick-dirty-fun co-op game unfurled itself into one of the most thoughtful videogames I've ever played, and easily my favourite of 2026 so far. I cannot even begin to explain what a fantastic job developer House House has done at creating an incredibly special, unreplicatable experience that has had me and my pals continuing to talk about it in the weeks since we rolled credits.

While so much of its exceptionality lies in its puzzles (and all of the little moments in between), one of the biggest things I fell in love with was its music. It's a surprisingly sporadic facet of the game—Big Walk doesn't have a soundtrack that accompanies you everywhere, and you can go some real chunky stretches of time without hearing any music at all.
points: Welcome to Critical Hit, where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.

articles.title: The World of Warcraft "Classic+" rumours were true and it's called World of Warcraft: Forever
articles.summary: Blizzard has officially confirmed World of Warcraft: Forever, the long-rumoured "Classic+" experience.
body: Last week, World of Warcraft fans were obsessing over colours as dataminers pulled hues from Blizzard's website that were labelled under a curious "wow 2" tag, leading many to speculate that this referred to the rumoured World of Warcraft Camelot, or as it's better known, "Classic Plus", much like how Blizzard is now expanding Diablo 2.
Now, following BlizzCon's opening ceremony, it turns out the rumours were pretty much bang on and World of Warcraft: Forever launches globally on 4th November.
If November sounds very far away, worry not; beta access begins this Thursday, 17th September, for anyone who's pre-purchased one of the game's upgrade packs.

A dedicated panel featuring senior game director Ion Hazzikostas, lead Classic designer Tim Jones, lead software engineer Nora Mills, and associate production director Clay Stone went into more detail on the new regions, systems, and design philosophy behind the project.
points: Blizzard has officially confirmed World of Warcraft: Forever, the long-rumoured "Classic+" experience.

articles.title: I've got a soft spot for cozy games with flying in them and these are my 4 favorites
articles.summary: I lobbied to make Promise Mascot Agency the best cozy game in our 2025 Game of the Year awards, which means I'm only ( checks calendar ) a little late in getting it added to my list of best cozy games this week.
body: It isn't even the only game with flying on the list now. It is in fact the third on that list of ten. I think I have a real soft spot for flying in cozy games.

There are as many definitions of "cozy game" as there are cozy gamers, but freedom is a really common element. There's freedom to build in life sims or freedom from time constraints in puzzle games. What is flying but complete and total freedom of exploration?

In the years since Breath of the Wild we've been spoiled for open world games with gliders, but a game with proper flying is even better. In Promise Mascot Agency I can hit my kei truck's boost thruster, nudge its nose up to gain altitude, and bank into a turn for a second pass over the rural sprawl below. It's the most open an open world can be and the freest I ever feel exploring one.

Once you upgrade your kei truck with wings you are unstoppable. This thing is meant to be bashed and crashed into every obstacle you find, which is extra true once you can launch it off a switchback mountain road into an elegant nose dive directly onto a collectible you were looking for. Pure joy.

articles.title: The weird, wonderful world of Miles Buckle, Instagram's parallel universe of video games
articles.summary: Going through Miles Buckle's Instagram feed is like stumbling into a parallel universe where cinema's greats – Lynch, Hitchcock, Fellini, Kubrick – are reimagined in the familiar but distinctly different visual language of video games.
body: For his university degree show last year, Buckle, who studied graphic communication design at Central St. Martin's in London, showed his final project, a short game called Nights Bridge, on a plastic-molded cream-griege desktop computer from the ancient times. "I bought a PC from the 90s off eBay," the 3D artist and animator tells me on a video call. "I took the parts out and put in modern hardware, so the monitor and the tower were like, 30 years old, and it had the keyboard and everything." He remembers all of it being obstinately heavy – it was a click-and-collect pickup situation, and he hauled it all home on foot.
